get.description: Only the host and confirmed attendees can call this. Both get the confirmed list; the host also gets the waitlist and the people holding an open offer, in queue order. Nobody else ever sees who is waitlisted or offered.

404.description: The caller is neither the host nor confirmed, or can't see the event.

delete.description: Gives up the caller's spot, place in the waitlist or open offer: while the caller holds an offer, this declines it. A freed spot is offered to the next person in the waitlist for the event's confirmWindowMinutes, or confirms them at once when the event starts sooner than that (D-014). Nobody is offered a spot once the event has started or is cancelled. Leaving without an RSVP is also a 204.

403.description: CSRF token missing or invalid. Send the XSRF-TOKEN cookie's value in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.

404.description: The event doesn't exist, or the caller can't see it (D-012). The host, and anyone confirmed or waitlisted, can still see it once it's cancelled.

409.description: errorType HOST_CANNOT_LEAVE: the host always holds a spot. They cancel the event instead.

post.description: Takes a free spot (CONFIRMED) or, when the event is full, the back of the waitlist (WAITLISTED, with a position). First come, first served: the claim is one atomic update, so the event is never overbooked. An unlimited event always confirms. Joining again while confirmed, waitlisted or offered returns the current status and changes nothing, so a double tap is safe. Someone who left, declined an offer or let one expire may join again, at the back of the queue (D-014). Checks run in this order: visibility (404), an existing RSVP (200 with its status, so the host always gets CONFIRMED), removal (RSVP_REMOVED), then the sign-up window (SIGNUP_NOT_OPEN, SIGNUP_CLOSED).

403.description: CSRF token missing or invalid. Send the XSRF-TOKEN cookie's value in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.

404.description: The event doesn't exist, or the caller can't see it (D-012). The host, and anyone confirmed or waitlisted, can still see it once it's cancelled.

409.description: errorType SIGNUP_NOT_OPEN: signupOpensAt hasn't come yet. SIGNUP_CLOSED: the event has started. RSVP_REMOVED: the host removed the caller, who can't rejoin.

429.description: Rate limited (errorType TOO_MANY_REQUESTS). Joins are limited to about one attempt per second per user, so wait before retrying.

post.description: Turns the caller's open offer into a confirmed spot (D-014). It works until offerExpiresAt, even if the expiry job hasn't run yet or the event has since started. Accepting again while confirmed returns CONFIRMED and changes nothing. Checks run in this order: visibility (404), already confirmed (200), an offer past its deadline or expired (OFFER_EXPIRED), then CONFIRMED for an open offer on a published event, and NO_OFFER otherwise.

404.description: The event doesn't exist, or the caller can't see it (D-012). The host, and anyone confirmed or waitlisted, can still see it once it's cancelled.

409.description: errorType OFFER_EXPIRED: the caller's offer ran out; they may join again, at the back of the queue. NO_OFFER: the caller holds no open offer: none was made, they declined it, or the event was cancelled.

delete.description: Takes away their spot or place in the waitlist, or their open offer, and they can't rejoin. They aren't notified. A freed spot goes to the next person in the waitlist, as for leaving. Removing someone who isn't signed up is also a 204, and writes nothing: they can still join. 404 unless the user is the host.

get.description: A small response for polling: about every 3 seconds in the 2 minutes around signupOpensAt, every 30 seconds otherwise, and not while the page is hidden. Anyone who can see the event can call it. myStatus, myPosition and offerExpiresAt are always the caller's own. Send the last ETag in If-None-Match to get a bodiless 304 while nothing the caller would see has changed. Responses are sent with Cache-Control: private, no-cache.

parameters.description: The ETag of the caller's last 200 from this endpoint.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

ETag.description: A tag for this response, which is specific to the caller. Send it back in If-None-Match.

304.description: Not modified: If-None-Match matches. No body.

post.description: The link holds a 128-bit random token, works once, and expires after 24 hours. This response is the only place the token appears: the server stores only its SHA-256. A user can have at most 20 unused, unexpired invites, and can't list or revoke them, so the client makes a new one only when the user asks for a new code, not each time a screen opens.

post.description: Send PushSubscription.toJSON(). An endpoint belongs to whoever subscribed with it last, so subscribing again moves it to the caller and replaces its keys; a browser shared between accounts never gets the previous user's pushes. A user has at most 10 subscriptions: an 11th replaces their oldest. This doesn't turn pushEnabled on (PATCH /api/me does).

confirmed.description: People holding a spot, in the order they joined, so the host comes first. Leaves out anyone who has blocked the caller or whom the caller has blocked.

offered.description: Only the host gets this: the people holding an open offer, in queue order (D-014). Their spots count as taken. Null for everyone else.

waitlist.description: Only the host gets this: the waitlist in queue order, next in line first. Null for everyone else.

label.description: The server, circle or person name. Null for FRIENDS, and for a server where the host is no longer discoverable, which then reaches no one.

errorType.description: The HTTP status name, or a domain type the operation documents for that status (D-011).

audience.description: 1 to 50 entries, each at most once.

capacity.description: The headcount, the host included (the host always holds a spot), so at least 2. Null for unlimited. An update can't make it smaller than the number already confirmed.

confirmWindowMinutes.description: How many minutes a freed spot is held for the next person in line to accept (D-014). Missing or null means 30 when creating and keeps the current window when editing. A change applies to later offers, not to open ones.

endsAt.description: After startsAt and at most 7 days later.

signupOpensAt.description: Before startsAt and at most a year earlier.

startsAt.description: In the future when creating, and within a year of now either way. An update may keep a start that has passed, but can't move the start into the past.

audience.description: Only the host gets this; it is null for everyone else.

capacity.description: The headcount, the host included. Null for unlimited.

confirmWindowMinutes.description: How many minutes a freed spot is held for the next person in line to accept (D-014).

location.description: Null when locationHidden: the location is CONFIRMED-only and the viewer is neither the host nor confirmed.

myStatus.description: Where the viewer stands. CONFIRMED for the host. The waitlist position and an offer's deadline are in GET /api/events/{eventId}/spots.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as cursor for the next, older page. Null on the last page.

unreadCount.description: Unread notifications in the whole inbox, not just this page. Capped at 100, so show 100 as 99+.

changes.description: EVENT_CHANGED only: what changed, at least one. The new location is never included.

eventTitle.description: The event's title when the notification was made. Set for every type but FRIEND_ACCEPTED.

friendId.description: FRIEND_ACCEPTED only: the new friend's user ID. Never their name: the client may look it up in GET /api/friends.

offerExpiresAt.description: SPOT_OFFERED only: when the offer runs out. Accept before then.

startsAt.description: EVENT_CHANGED (the start after the change) and EVENT_REMINDER only.

upTo.description: The newest notification ID the caller has seen. It and every older one of the caller's own are marked read; newer ones stay unread.

eventId.description: The event's public ID. Null for FRIEND_ACCEPTED.

id.description: Higher for newer notifications. Send it as upTo to POST /api/notifications/read.

publicKey.description: The VAPID public key: an uncompressed P-256 point (65 bytes), base64url without padding. Pass it as applicationServerKey to pushManager.subscribe().

p256dh.description: The browser's P-256 public key (65 bytes), base64url.

endpoint.description: An https URL on a known push service: FCM (Chrome and most Chromium browsers), Mozilla, Apple or Windows (WNS). Any other host is a 400, so the server never sends requests anywhere else.

offerExpiresAt.description: When the caller's offer runs out. Null unless OFFERED.

position.description: 1-based place in the waitlist: 1 + the number of people waitlisted ahead of the caller. Null unless WAITLISTED.

capacity.description: The headcount, the host included. Null for unlimited.

confirmed.description: People holding a spot, the host included. A spot held by an open offer counts (D-014).

myPosition.description: The caller's own 1-based place in the waitlist: 1 + the number of people waitlisted ahead of them. Null unless myStatus is WAITLISTED.

offerExpiresAt.description: When the caller's own offer runs out. Null unless myStatus is OFFERED.

spotsLeft.description: capacity - confirmed. Null for unlimited. Nobody is promoted once the event has started, so this can be above 0 while people are waitlisted; sign-up is closed by then.

guilds.description: One entry per server; a guildId may appear only once.

pushEnabled.description: Whether new notifications are also pushed to the user's subscribed browsers (D-014). Off, they still reach the inbox, and subscriptions are kept. Subscribing a browser doesn't turn this on: the client sends both.

session.description: Session cookie set by Discord sign-in. Every request other than GET must also send the XSRF-TOKEN cookie's value in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.
